en: The national bird, the Philippine eagle, has a wingspan of up to two meters and weighs about eight kilograms.
The Philippine flag features three five-pointed stars representing the country's three main island groups: Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao.
The legislative branch, called Congress, is divided into the Senate with 24 members and the House of Representatives with over 300 members.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but Filipino and English are the two official languages used in government and schools.
The Sinulog festival in Cebu celebrates the Santo Niño with a traditional dance pattern of nine steps forward and one step backward.
Jose Rizal was only 35 years old when he was executed by firing squad at Bagumbayan on December 30, 1896.
The indigenous Ifugao people carved the Banaue Rice Terraces into mountains 1,500 meters above sea level over 2,000 years ago.
Dr. Fe del Mundo founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines in 1957, dedicating over 70 years of her life to medicine.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old to vote, and at least 35 years old to run for President.
National Artist Napoleon Abueva created over 500 sculptures during his lifetime, earning him the title Father of Modern Philippine Sculpture.
The national flower Sampaguita grows up to three meters tall and produces white flowers with a diameter of two to three centimeters.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution, the current supreme law of the land, contains exactly 18 articles detailing the government structure and bill of rights.
